# ── Mapping Model Probabilities to Flag Categories ────────────────────────────
#
# The ML model predicts a probability of default for each customer.
# The Invisible Debt Trap Flag is the business-facing output. It converts
# the predicted probability into a simple risk category that a user can
# understand: Stable, Watch, Early Flag, or High Risk.
#
# For this demonstration, we use the Classification Tree because it achieved
# the strongest recall among the tested models. Recall is important here
# because the project is designed as an early warning system, where missing
# a genuinely risky customer is more harmful than flagging too cautiously.
#
# The probability bands are estimated from the training prediction distribution
# and then applied to the test set. This avoids designing the flag thresholds
# directly from the test data.
#
# These bands are demonstration thresholds only. A real Australian system
# would need calibration using local customer-consented data from statements
# or CDR/open banking.
#
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


# Step 1 — Get predicted probabilities from the Classification Tree
# We already have pred_tree_prob from model training
# Column "Default" contains the probability of default for each customer

default_probs_test <- pred_tree_prob[, "Default"]

cat("Predicted probability summary on test set:\n")
## Predicted probability summary on test set:
print(summary(default_probs_test))
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##  0.2690  0.2690  0.3967  0.4390  0.6185  0.8866
cat("\n")
# Step 2 — Get training predictions to set probability band thresholds
# We use the saved cross-validation predictions from the training phase
# This ensures our bands are defined from training data, not test data

train_cv_probs <- model_tree$pred %>%
  filter(cp == model_tree$bestTune$cp) %>%
  pull(Default)

# If CV predictions are not available, use training set predictions directly
if (length(train_cv_probs) == 0) {
  train_cv_probs <- predict(model_tree,
                             newdata = train_data,
                             type    = "prob")[, "Default"]
}

cat("Training probability distribution (used to set band thresholds):\n")
## Training probability distribution (used to set band thresholds):
print(quantile(train_cv_probs,
               probs = c(0.25, 0.40, 0.60, 0.75, 0.90)))
##       25%       40%       60%       75%       90% 
## 0.2703956 0.2719926 0.4010233 0.6147748 0.8855693
cat("\n")
# Step 3 — Define probability bands from training distribution
# We use natural breaks in the training probability distribution
# rather than arbitrary fixed values

threshold_watch      <- round(quantile(train_cv_probs, 0.40), 3)
threshold_early_flag <- round(quantile(train_cv_probs, 0.65), 3)
threshold_high_risk  <- round(quantile(train_cv_probs, 0.82), 3)

cat("Probability band thresholds (from training distribution):\n")
## Probability band thresholds (from training distribution):
cat("Stable:     probability < ", threshold_watch, "\n")
## Stable:     probability <  0.272
cat("Watch:      probability ", threshold_watch,
    "to <", threshold_early_flag, "\n")
## Watch:      probability  0.272 to < 0.404
cat("Early Flag: probability ", threshold_early_flag,
    "to <", threshold_high_risk, "\n")
## Early Flag: probability  0.404 to < 0.653
cat("High Risk:  probability >=", threshold_high_risk, "\n\n")
## High Risk:  probability >= 0.653
# Step 4 — Apply thresholds to test set probabilities
test_flag_mapped <- data.frame(
  Actual_Default = test_data$DEFAULT,
  Default_Prob   = default_probs_test
) %>%
  mutate(
    ML_Flag = case_when(
      Default_Prob >= threshold_high_risk  ~ "High Risk",
      Default_Prob >= threshold_early_flag ~ "Early Flag",
      Default_Prob >= threshold_watch      ~ "Watch",
      TRUE                                 ~ "Stable"
    ),
    ML_Flag = factor(ML_Flag,
                     levels  = c("Stable", "Watch",
                                 "Early Flag", "High Risk"),
                     ordered = TRUE)
  )


# Step 5 — Check flag distribution and default rates per flag
cat("=== ML PROBABILITY FLAG DISTRIBUTION ===\n\n")
## === ML PROBABILITY FLAG DISTRIBUTION ===
flag_summary <- test_flag_mapped %>%
  group_by(ML_Flag) %>%
  summarise(
    Customers    = n(),
    Pct          = round(n() / nrow(test_flag_mapped) * 100, 1),
    Avg_Prob     = round(mean(Default_Prob) * 100, 1),
    Default_Rate = round(mean(Actual_Default == "Default") * 100, 1)
  )

print(flag_summary)
## # A tibble: 4 × 5
##   ML_Flag    Customers   Pct Avg_Prob Default_Rate
##   <ord>          <int> <dbl>    <dbl>        <dbl>
## 1 Stable          4044  45       26.9          9.5
## 2 Watch           1856  20.6     39.3         14.7
## 3 Early Flag      1614  18       55.7         25.8
## 4 High Risk       1475  16.4     83.3         62.1
cat("\n")
cat("Note: Default rate should increase from Stable to High Risk.\n")
## Note: Default rate should increase from Stable to High Risk.
cat("This validates that probability bands are meaningful.\n")
## This validates that probability bands are meaningful.
# ── Visualising the Probability-to-Flag Mapping ───────────────────────────────
#
# Two charts side by side:
# Left: distribution of predicted probabilities coloured by flag category
# Right: default rate per flag category with customer counts
#
# Together they show both HOW the probabilities are distributed AND
# whether the flag categories are genuinely separating risk levels.
#
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

flag_colours <- c("Stable"     = "#27AE60",
                  "Watch"      = "#F39C12",
                  "Early Flag" = "#E67E22",
                  "High Risk"  = "#C0392B")

# ── Left chart — probability distribution by flag ────────────────────────────

p_left <- ggplot(test_flag_mapped,
                 aes(x = Default_Prob, fill = ML_Flag)) +

  geom_histogram(bins     = 40,
                 colour   = "white",
                 linewidth = 0.2) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = threshold_watch,
             linetype   = "dashed",
             colour     = "grey40",
             linewidth  = 0.7) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = threshold_early_flag,
             linetype   = "dashed",
             colour     = "grey40",
             linewidth  = 0.7) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = threshold_high_risk,
             linetype   = "dashed",
             colour     = "grey40",
             linewidth  = 0.7) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = flag_colours) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(round(x * 100), "%"),
    limits = c(0.2, 0.95)
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +

  labs(
    title    = "Predicted Default Probability Distribution",
    subtitle = "Colour shows assigned flag category",
    x        = "Predicted Probability of Default",
    y        = "Number of Customers",
    fill     = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# ── Right chart — default rate by flag with counts ───────────────────────────

p_right <- flag_summary %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = ML_Flag, y = Default_Rate, fill = ML_Flag)) +

  geom_bar(stat   = "identity",
           width  = 0.55,
           colour = "white") +

  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Default_Rate, "%\n(n=", comma(Customers), ")")),
            vjust    = -0.3,
            size     = 3.5,
            fontface = "bold") +

  scale_fill_manual(values = flag_colours) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 75),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
  ) +

  labs(
    title    = "Default Rate by Flag Category",
    subtitle = "Validates probability bands are meaningful",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Actual Default Rate (%)",
    fill     = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position    = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank()
  )


# ── Combine both charts ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

grid.arrange(
  p_left, p_right,
  ncol = 2,
  top  = grid::textGrob(
    "Invisible Debt Trap Flag — Probability Mapping Validation",
    gp = grid::gpar(fontface = "bold", fontsize = 13)
  )
)

# ── Detection Gap Chart ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# This chart makes the core novelty argument of the project with real data.
#
# Part A — Calibration diagram:
# Shows that as the model's predicted probability rises, actual default
# rates rise in lockstep. This proves the model is capturing genuine risk.
# The shaded zones show where the Invisible Debt Trap Flag categories sit.
#
# Part B — Detection gap comparison:
# Compares two detection approaches on the same test set:
# 1. Traditional proxy: only flags customers already missing payments
#    (PAY_DELAY_COUNT >= 2 — equivalent to ASIC serious delinquency)
# 2. Our AI early warning: flags Watch and Early Flag customers who
#    have ZERO payment delays — the invisible stressed customers that
#    traditional monitoring completely misses
#
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


# ── Step 1: Add PAY_DELAY_COUNT back into the mapped test set ─────────────────

test_flag_mapped$PAY_DELAY_COUNT <- test_data$PAY_DELAY_COUNT


# ── Step 2: Create 10 probability bands and calculate actual default rates ────

calibration_data <- test_flag_mapped %>%
  mutate(
    Prob_Band = cut(Default_Prob,
                   breaks = seq(0.25, 0.95, by = 0.07),
                   include.lowest = TRUE,
                   right          = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Prob_Band) %>%
  summarise(
    Customers    = n(),
    Actual_Rate  = round(mean(Actual_Default == "Default") * 100, 1),
    Avg_Prob     = round(mean(Default_Prob) * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Prob_Band))

cat("Calibration data by probability band:\n")
## Calibration data by probability band:
print(calibration_data)
## # A tibble: 7 × 4
##   Prob_Band   Customers Actual_Rate Avg_Prob
##   <fct>           <int>       <dbl>    <dbl>
## 1 [0.25,0.32)      4087         9.6     26.9
## 2 [0.32,0.39)        53        17       32.8
## 3 [0.39,0.46)      2183        15.3     40  
## 4 [0.53,0.6)        371        25.9     58.5
## 5 [0.6,0.67)        820        29.5     61.9
## 6 [0.74,0.81)       537        46.7     74.1
## 7 [0.88,0.95]       938        70.9     88.7
cat("\n")
# ── Step 3: Part A — Calibration reliability diagram ─────────────────────────

p_calibration <- ggplot(calibration_data,
                         aes(x = Avg_Prob, y = Actual_Rate)) +

  # Shaded zones
  annotate("rect", xmin = 25, xmax = 40,
           ymin = 0, ymax = 100,
           alpha = 0.07, fill = "#27AE60") +

  annotate("rect", xmin = 40, xmax = 62,
           ymin = 0, ymax = 100,
           alpha = 0.07, fill = "#F39C12") +

  annotate("rect", xmin = 62, xmax = 95,
           ymin = 0, ymax = 100,
           alpha = 0.08, fill = "#C0392B") +

  # Zone labels
  annotate("text", x = 33, y = 90,
           label = "Stable\nZone",
           size = 3, colour = "#27AE60", fontface = "bold") +

  annotate("text", x = 51, y = 90,
           label = "Early\nWarning\nZone",
           size = 3, colour = "#E67E22", fontface = "bold") +

  annotate("text", x = 78, y = 90,
           label = "High\nRisk\nZone",
           size = 3, colour = "#C0392B", fontface = "bold") +

  # Perfect calibration reference line
  geom_abline(slope     = 1,
              intercept = 0,
              linetype  = "dashed",
              colour    = "grey60",
              linewidth = 0.8) +

  # Actual calibration line
  geom_line(colour    = "#2C3E50",
            linewidth = 1.2) +

  geom_point(aes(size = Customers),
             colour = "#2C3E50",
             alpha  = 0.85) +

  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Actual_Rate, "%")),
            vjust  = -1.2,
            size   = 3.2,
            colour = "#2C3E50",
            fontface = "bold") +

  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 9), guide = "none") +

  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(25, 95),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +

  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +

  labs(
    title    = "Model Calibration — Predicted vs Actual Default Rate",
    subtitle = "Each point = one probability band | Point size = number of customers",
    x        = "Predicted Default Probability (%)",
    y        = "Actual Default Rate (%)",
    caption  = "Dashed line = perfect calibration"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


# ── Step 4: Part B — Detection gap comparison ─────────────────────────────────
#
# We compare two groups:
# Group 1 — Traditional proxy: PAY_DELAY_COUNT >= 2
#            These customers are already missing payments
#            Traditional monitoring catches them here
#
# Group 2 — AI early warning gap: Watch or Early Flag with zero delays
#            These customers show behavioural stress but no missed payments yet
#            Traditional monitoring completely misses these customers

traditional_group <- test_flag_mapped %>%
  filter(PAY_DELAY_COUNT >= 2)

ai_gap_group <- test_flag_mapped %>%
  filter(ML_Flag %in% c("Watch", "Early Flag"),
         PAY_DELAY_COUNT == 0)

comparison_data <- data.frame(
  Group        = c("Traditional Proxy\n(PAY_DELAY >= 2)",
                   "AI Early Warning Gap\n(Watch/Early Flag, no delays)"),
  Customers    = c(nrow(traditional_group), nrow(ai_gap_group)),
  Default_Rate = c(
    round(mean(traditional_group$Actual_Default == "Default") * 100, 1),
    round(mean(ai_gap_group$Actual_Default    == "Default") * 100, 1)
  ),
  Type = c("Traditional", "AI Gap")
)

cat("Detection gap comparison:\n")
## Detection gap comparison:
print(comparison_data)

## 1                 Traditional Proxy\n(PAY_DELAY >= 2)      1680         53.4
## 2 AI Early Warning Gap\n(Watch/Early Flag, no delays)      1911         15.9

## 1 Traditional
## 2      AI Gap
cat("\n")
cat("AI early warning gap customers — invisible to traditional systems:\n")
## AI early warning gap customers — invisible to traditional systems:
cat("Total customers our system catches early:", nrow(ai_gap_group), "\n")
## Total customers our system catches early: 1911
cat("Their actual default rate:", comparison_data$Default_Rate[2], "%\n")
## Their actual default rate: 15.9 %
cat("Without our system these customers receive no warning\n\n")
## Without our system these customers receive no warning
p_gap <- ggplot(comparison_data,
                aes(x = Group, y = Customers, fill = Type)) +

  geom_bar(stat   = "identity",
           width  = 0.5,
           colour = "white") +

  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(comma(Customers),
                                "\ncustomers\n(",
                                Default_Rate, "% default)")),
            vjust    = -0.3,
            size     = 3.5,
            fontface = "bold") +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Traditional" = "#AEB6BF",
                                "AI Gap"      = "#2471A3")) +

  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma,
                     limits = c(0, max(comparison_data$Customers) * 1.35)) +

  labs(
    title    = "Detection Gap — What Traditional Systems Miss",
    subtitle = "Blue = customers our AI system catches before any payment delay occurs",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Number of Customers",
    caption  = "Traditional proxy = PAY_DELAY_COUNT >= 2 | AI gap = Watch/Early Flag with zero delays"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position    = "none",
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank()
  )


# ── Step 5: Combine both charts ───────────────────────────────────────────────

grid.arrange(
  p_calibration, p_gap,
  ncol = 2,
  top  = grid::textGrob(
    "Invisible Debt Trap Analytics — Detection Gap Evidence",
    gp = grid::gpar(fontface = "bold", fontsize = 13)
  )
)
